title: Normalized integral fraction for an integral rational series
statement:
Let $Z(T)\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]$ be rational over $\mathbf Q$.
Then $Z$ has a unique
normalized reduced
integral presentation: there are unique $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$
such that $A(0)=B(0)=1$, $\gcd(A,B)=1$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$,
and $BZ=A$.

proof.text: Write $Z=\sum_{n\geq0}z_nT^n$ with $z_n\in\mathbf Z$, $z_0=1$. By hypothesis $Z$, regarded in $\mathbf Q[[T]]$, is rational [def-weil-rational-power-series]: there are $P,Q\in\mathbf Q[T]$ with $Q(0)\neq0$ and $QZ=P$; replacing $(P,Q)$ by $(Q(0)^{-1}P,Q(0)^{-1}Q)$ we may take $Q(0)=1$. For $m\geq0$ let $R_m=(z_{m+s})_{s\geq0}\in\mathbf Q^{\mathbf Z_{\geq0}}$ be the $m$-th shifted coefficient sequence and $V\subseteq\mathbf Q^{\mathbf Z_{\geq0}}$ the $\mathbf Q$-span of all $R_m$ [def-weil-sequence-subspace]. By [lem-weil-rational-series-finite-shift-span] (with $K=\mathbf Q$, $f=Z$), $V$ is finite-dimensional [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace].

source.place: Ch. II §27, Cor. 27.8 and proof of Lemma 27.9, pp. 156-157 (rationality over $\mathbf Q$ as a linear recurrence of the coefficients, Bourbaki Algèbre IV §5 Ex. 3(a)); blueprint ## Proof, first paragraph

proof.text: Let $L\subseteq V$ be the subgroup of $\mathbf Q^{\mathbf Z_{\geq0}}$ generated by the $R_m$, $m\geq0$ (finite $\mathbf Z$-linear combinations). (i) Every $v\in L$ has integer coordinates, since each $R_m$ has ($R_m(s)=z_{m+s}\in\mathbf Z$) and sums and integer multiples preserve this. (ii) The left shift $S(v)_s=v_{s+1}$ is additive and $S(R_m)=R_{m+1}$, so $S(L)\subseteq L$. (iii) $R_0\in L$ and $R_0(0)=z_0=1$.

$L$ is a free abelian group of finite rank. By [lem-weil-finite-coordinate-detection] applied to the finite-dimensional space $V$ (step 1) there is a finite set $J\subseteq\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ such that $v\mapsto(v_j)_{j\in J}$ is injective on $V$, hence on $L\subseteq V$. By (i) of step 2 this map sends $L$ into $\mathbf Z^J$, and it is additive; so $L$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of $\mathbf Z^J$, hence by [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free] free of finite rank $r\leq|J|$. By (iii) $L\neq0$, so $r\geq1$.

Let $S_L:L\to L$ be the restriction of $S$ (step 2 (ii)), a $\mathbf Z$-linear endomorphism of the free $\mathbf Z$-module $L$ of rank $r$ (step 3), and $C(T)=\sum_{i=0}^rc_iT^i=\det(T\,I_r-M)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] its characteristic polynomial, $M$ the integer matrix of $S_L$ in a basis of $L$. By Cayley–Hamilton [lem-weil-cayley-hamilton-free-module], $C$ is monic of degree $r$ ($c_r=1$) and $\sum_{i=0}^rc_iS_L^i=0$. Applying this to $R_0\in L$ and using $S^i(R_0)=R_i$ gives $\sum_{i=0}^rc_iR_i=0$, whose $s$-th coordinate is the integral linear recurrence $\sum_{i=0}^rc_iz_{s+i}=0$ for all $s\geq0$.

source.place: ## Proof, third paragraph (integer matrix $M$ of $S|_L$, $z_n=eM^nv$); in this form the slopmaster2 Lean exists_monic_sum_coeff_mul_eq_zero, WeilConjectures/ZetaLinearAlgebra/IntegralRecurrence.lean lines 147-184

proof.text: Integral presentation with constant terms one. Let $B_0=\operatorname{rev}(C)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ be the reverse of $C$ [def-weil-reverse-polynomial]. By [lem-weil-reverse-polynomial-coefficients], $[T^j]B_0=c_{r-j}$ for $0\leq j\leq r$ and $0$ for $j>r$ [def-weil-polynomial-coefficient]; so $B_0(0)=c_r=1$, and for every $N\geq r$ the coefficient of $T^N$ in $B_0Z$ (with $B_0$ regarded as a power series [def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series]) is $\sum_{j=0}^rc_{r-j}z_{N-j}=\sum_{i=0}^rc_iz_{(N-r)+i}=0$ by step 4 with $s=N-r$. Hence $B_0Z=A_0$ in $\mathbf Z[[T]]$, where $A_0=\sum_{N<r}([T^N](B_0Z))T^N\in\mathbf Z[T]$, and $A_0(0)=B_0(0)z_0=1$. (This replaces the blueprint's $A_0=e\,\mathrm{adj}(I-TM)v$, $B_0=\det(I-TM)$, which is the same $B_0$.)

source.place: ## Proof, fourth paragraph (gcd $G$ of $A_0,B_0$, normalized by $G(0)=\pm1$)

proof.text: Normalized Gauss lemma: if $F\in\mathbf Z[T]$ with $F(0)=1$, and $G\in\mathbf Q[T]$ with $G(0)=1$ divides the image of $F$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$, then $G$ has integer coefficients. Proof: write $F=GH$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$ (we identify $F$ with its image, which has the same coefficients and degree since $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Q$ is injective [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map]); $\mathbf Q[T]$ is a domain, so $\deg F=\deg G+\deg H$, and [lem-weil-polynomial-reflection-multiplicative] with $N_1=\deg G$, $N_2=\deg H$ gives $\operatorname{rev}(F)=\operatorname{rev}(G)\operatorname{rev}(H)$ [def-weil-reverse-polynomial]. By [lem-weil-reverse-polynomial-coefficients], $[T^{\deg F}]\operatorname{rev}(F)=F(0)=1$ is the top coefficient, so $\operatorname{rev}(F)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ is monic; likewise $\operatorname{rev}(G)\in\mathbf Q[T]$ is monic. By [lem-weil-monic-divisor-integral], $\operatorname{rev}(G)$ has integer coefficients; since $[T^j]\operatorname{rev}(G)=[T^{\deg G-j}]G$ for $0\leq j\leq\deg G$ (again [lem-weil-reverse-polynomial-coefficients]), every coefficient of $G$ is a coefficient of $\operatorname{rev}(G)$, so $G$ has integer coefficients. Apply this to $(F,G)=(A_0,A')$ and $(B_0,B')$ (step 6: $A'\mid a$, $B'\mid b$): $A'$, $B'$ are the images of $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$ with $A(0)=B(0)=1$.

proof.text: The identity $BZ=A$. From step 6, $aB'=hA'B'=bA'$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$, i.e. the images of $A_0B$ and $B_0A$ agree, so $A_0B=B_0A$ in $\mathbf Z[T]$ ($\mathbf Z[T]\to\mathbf Q[T]$ is injective [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map]). In $\mathbf Z[[T]]$ [def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series], using step 5: $B_0\cdot(BZ)=(B_0Z)B=A_0B=B_0A$. Since $B_0(0)=1$, $B_0$ is a unit of $\mathbf Z[[T]]$ [lem-weil-power-series-unit-constant-coefficient]; multiplying by $B_0^{-1}$ gives $BZ=A$.

proof.text: Existence. By steps 6-8, $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$ satisfy $A(0)=B(0)=1$, their images $A',B'$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$ are coprime, and $BZ=A$: $(A,B)$ is a normalized reduced integral presentation of $Z$ [def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction].

source.place: §1, proof of (1.7)⇒(1.6), p. 276 ("D'après un lemme de Fatou ... les termes constants de P et Q sont 1"); Milne LEC Prop. 27.11, p. 158

proof.text: Uniqueness. Let $(A,B)$ and $(A_2,B_2)$ be two normalized reduced integral presentations [def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction]. In $\mathbf Z[[T]]$: $A_2B=(B_2Z)B=B_2(BZ)=B_2A$; the map $\mathbf Z[T]\to\mathbf Z[[T]]$ is injective [def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series], so $A_2B=B_2A$ in $\mathbf Z[T]$, hence in $\mathbf Q[T]$ [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map]. There $A\mid A_2B$ with $A,B$ coprime [def-weil-coprime-polynomials], so $A\mid A_2$ by [lem-weil-coprime-divides-product]; symmetrically $A_2\mid B_2A$ with $A_2,B_2$ coprime gives $A_2\mid A$. Write $A_2=uA$, $A=vA_2$; as $A\neq0$ ($A(0)=1$) and $\mathbf Q[T]$ is a domain, $uv=1$, so $\deg u=\deg v=0$ and $u$ is a nonzero constant; comparing constant terms, $1=u\cdot1$, so $A_2=A$. Then $AB=B_2A$ and cancelling $A\neq0$ gives $B_2=B$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$, hence in $\mathbf Z[T]$.
